column7: The fourth Wu-Tang album. Feels looser and more upbeat than The W, with a return to some of the classic Wu energy. The production leans heavier on horn stabs, military-style drums, and funk samples–less gritty then earlier stuff. ODB is mostly absent, and Cappadonna had fallen out with the group, but it still clicks in places.

column7:
The seventh Wu-Tang album. A whole different approach—recorded in secret with only one physical copy ever made, at least that was the original thought. It is expected there are about 5000 bootlegs of the album out there. Produced by Cilvaringz, it’s darker and more introspective, with a unique mix of experimental sounds. He blends old-school Wu with something more cinematic and atmospheric. The whole thing became a cultural artifact, especially after the wild story of Shkreli owning it and nearly destroying it. This album is probably the biggest grail in unreleased hip-hop music history.
